analysis.title: Global Equity Strategy: Barclays Equity Factor Insights: October 2026
key_insights: US factor views unchanged: Positive Value, Neutral Growth, Positive Large-over-Small, Neutral Momentum, Neutral Quality, Negative High-over-Low Volatility, Neutral Yield. Sticky inflation and rising rates favor Value vs Growth and Large vs Small.

US Value case: inflation above target, growth holding up, tighter financial conditions. Widening credit spreads across hyperscaler, data center and neo-cloud issuers and higher hyperscaler CDS spreads, with Treasury yields sharply higher. Investor fatigue with the crowded AI narrative could help under-owned segments. Value is described as an 'anti-AI' style factor.
Current earnings growth concentration may be vulnerable to downward revisions in semiconductors, which have shown some of the largest forecast errors among S&P 500 industry groups.

US Large-over-Small: since end of 1H26 the Russell 2000 and S&P 600 have fallen more than 7% while the S&P 500 gained 4.0%. The 10-year Treasury yield moved above 5%. Barclays rates strategists expect the 10-year to stay around current levels for several quarters. Small-cap leverage is near post-COVID highs and the share of unprofitable companies is elevated (33% of the Russell 2000 per Figure 24).

In September the S&P 500 fell 0.5%, with Banks (-7.3%) and Capital Markets (-9.9%) offsetting AI strength. Semiconductors gained 7.2% and Big Tech 8.1%. Small caps fell 5.4%. Russell 1000 Growth +2.1% vs Russell 1000 Value -3.3%.

Past-month US factor moves: Growth beat Value by 5.3%, Momentum gained roughly 10% (10.1% since end of August), and Large-over-Small gained 3.4%. Semis, Electrical Equipment and weak Software drove about half of Momentum's return.

US Momentum stays Neutral: AI and energy strength, Middle East geopolitical risk and cheap valuation vs own history (cheapest of the styles tracked) are offset by midterm election risk. In almost every midterm year since 2006 Momentum sold off from the start of October through the end of November (four of the last five per Figure 30).

US Quality stays Neutral: FY27 earnings forecasts imply mid-teens growth. Semiconductors are more than 70% of expected earnings growth, and even a significant downward revision would leave growth in double digits. Quality has historically outperformed around midterm elections.

US High-over-Low Volatility stays Negative: the factor has the lowest share of profitable companies among styles, historically struggles in drawdowns, and faces elevated rates and midterm uncertainty.

US Yield stays Neutral: high risk-free rates cut the appeal of dividends and buybacks, but Yield is under-owned and acts as an 'anti-AI' style with exposure to Banks, Insurance, Oil & Gas and Software & IT Services, so a broadening of leadership would help.
Growth is the most crowded US style versus its own 10-year history (88th percentile), followed by Value at 83%. Barclays projects annual AI infrastructure spend above $1.4 trillion by 2028.

Europe: Positive Value; Neutral Growth, Small Caps, Momentum and Low Vol; Negative Quality. Value's rate tailwind from higher Bund yields has been offset by wider Euro Area sovereign spreads on French fiscal concerns. Narrower spreads as French political risk stabilizes would support Value.

Europe earnings: positive EU CESI points to a broad beat rate across STOXX 600, with historical 60/70% of companies beating EPS in high-CESI periods. Broad beats have historically favored Value, Growth and Small Caps.

Europe Momentum: crowding in high-Momentum stocks is at 2-year lows, so the factor is more sensitive to AI upside. Earnings momentum remains weak. Momentum led over the past month but has moved into 'fading' on the factor-pair regime map.

Europe performance since September: Momentum and Yield led, Volatility lagged, Quality and Size were broadly flat, Growth and Value were slightly negative. Yield is the leader on the long side over three months.
Europe seasonality: October historically favors Vol and Value, while Momentum and Quality lag (median Oct Quality -1.3%, Momentum -0.2%).

sector_views.rationale: Energy reversed its 2Q26 losses with a 16.5% gain in 3Q26 and is a large Momentum long tilt; Value and Yield also have Oil & Gas exposure.
Semis drove Growth and Momentum returns (+7.2% in September) but account for more than 70% of expected earnings growth and carry downward revision risk.
Banks fell 7.3% and Capital Markets 9.9% in September; Value basket is tilted toward Financials.
Utilities lost 13% in 3Q26 as yields rose.

earnings_insights: FY27 US earnings forecasts imply mid-teens growth (Barclays forecasts); semiconductors are more than 70% of expected earnings growth, and a significant downward revision would still leave aggregate growth in double digits.
Small cap EPS growth is expected to pick up in coming quarters (Figure 22); small cap earnings revisions are near parity with large caps but lag Tech.
EU: positive CESI points to a broad STOXX 600 beat rate of 60/70% of companies beating EPS expectations in the coming earnings season (historical relationship, a forecast not a print).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield above the 5% threshold pressures small caps and financing conditions and favors Large over Small and Value over Growth.

macro_indicators.reading: around current levels for the next several quarters
macro_indicators.interpretation: Barclays rates strategists expect elevated yields to persist, keeping the environment challenging for small caps.

macro_indicators.reading: between one and two hikes priced by 2026YE; implied mid-2027 policy rate up 60 bps in two months
macro_indicators.interpretation: A potential headwind for small caps.
Supports a sticky-inflation backdrop favorable to Value.

trade_ideas.description: Long US Value factor basket over Growth
trade_ideas.rationale: Sticky inflation, tighter financial conditions and AI-narrative fatigue favor broadening to under-owned segments.
trade_ideas.risk: Continued AI leadership and semiconductor earnings strength.

trade_ideas.description: Long US large caps over small caps
trade_ideas.rationale: Yields above 5% and weak small-cap balance sheets pressure smaller companies.
trade_ideas.risk: A fall in rates or small-cap earnings pickup.

trade_ideas.description: Underweight US High-over-Low Volatility (favor low-vol stocks)
trade_ideas.rationale: Lowest share of profitable companies among styles, struggles in drawdowns.

trade_ideas.description: Long EU Value factor; Negative on EU Quality
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher-for-longer rates, stronger earnings revisions, narrowing sovereign spreads as French risk stabilizes.

risk_factors: US midterm elections could disrupt trends and raise factor volatility.
10-year yield staying above 5% and rate hikes being priced.
Hyperscaler credit spread and CDS widening amid heavy issuance.
Renewed fiscal concerns in France and wider Euro Area spreads.
ECB reinforcing a higher-for-longer message would hurt EU Growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Value benefits from sticky inflation, resilient growth and AI-narrative fatigue as leadership broadens beyond crowded AI winners.
tension_points.bear_case: AI remains the primary driver: Growth outperformed Value by 5.3% in the past month on semiconductor and Big Tech strength.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upside to semiconductor earnings and continued AI leadership would undercut broadening; the report flags downward semiconductor revisions as what would help Value.

tension_points.bull_case: AI and energy strength, Middle East risk and cheap relative valuation support Momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: In four of the last five midterm years Momentum sold off from September-end to November-end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Midterm election disruption of prevailing trends between October and November.
